title: The 1957 bust, Rikers Island, and Woody Herman
summary: He served four months, then joined Woody Herman's small band and was struck on the chops.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: Well, you're in New York and you've gotten the habit.
Yeah. Well, I suffered with that up until '37, and I got busted...
No, I mean '57, yeah. Well, that's where we
were, right? Did I say '37? I slipped.

Yeah, I got busted, and I went to Riker's Island for four months. And I did that, and when I came out then I cleaned up. Then I got a gig with Woody Herman in his small band, and we went to Washington D.C., and some cat... Boy, I don't know, some cat was dancing with this girl and he stuck his hand out, and I wasn't looking at the floor, at the particular thing, and he hit me right in the chops, man...

He hit my horn while I was playing. And that's like a razor cutting you when somebody hits you, especially when you don't expect it. I had a hell of a time trying to get my chops back and keep working.
What did you do for that?
Well, first I had to lay off that the rest of the night.

Yeah. And rest my chops, hoping that they would heal by the next night so I can use them -- which I did. Thank goodness, I always had good chops. But I'm talking so much about me and my feelings. That ain't necessary, is it?
